rationale: Evidence from iteration 7 (score 712.2, best so far): the oval finishes 20/20 (1.97 s), and the s-bend now finishes 20/20 (2.19 s). The slalom is still 0/20. Its progress rose from 0.16 to 0.56 and it leaves the track more slowly, with 0.25 line-loss events per run, and every run ends off_track at max_error about 0.063 m. Iteration 7 changed three things together (base_speed 1.0 to 0.9, body_length 0.18 to 0.14, mass 0.8 to 0.7). Yaw inertia scales with (body_length^2 + body_width^2)/12 times mass, so this cut inertia by roughly 25 percent. The slalom gain points to the robot's inability to turn quickly enough and to recover from fast direction changes, not to sensing reach, since widening the array in iteration 6 did not move the slalom. Off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.12/4) = 0.06 m for this body, and widening the body to 0.18 m would not raise it (0.0575 < 0.06), so the body width stays at 0.12 m. Change: continue the same direction. base_speed drops from 0.9 to 0.8, body_length from 0.14 to 0.12 m (near the 0.10 minimum), and mass from 0.7 to 0.6 kg, reducing inertia by a further ~20 percent. Sensors, weights, kp 6.5, kd 2.0, ki 0.2 and line_loss are unchanged. Expected result: slalom progress above 0.7 with some finishes, and line-loss events below 0.25 per run. The oval and s-bend should still finish, at about 2.0 to 2.3 s, costing only a few points of time score. Risks: lower speed may slow the oval and s-bend, and a short, light body may be less stable on straights, so watch steering_oscillation (currently 0.19 oval, 0.27 s-bend, 0.35 slalom). If the oval oscillates above 0.4, the next step is kd 1.7. If the slalom still exits on its first swing with progress under 0.7, the next step is kp 7.0 with kd 2.2. Hypotheses: H1, slalom failure is turning agility limited by inertia and speed, so further reduction helps. H2, kp and kd are now adequate for the lower inertia, so the slalom should respond without retuning. Measurements wanted next: progress, completion and max_error per track to see how far the slalom runs get and how much margin is used, line_loss_events on the slalom, steering_oscillation for chatter from the lighter body, and completion_time on the oval and s-bend to check the speed cost.
